This Emerging Artist Is a Hit Restaurateur

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2171 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Borgo sits on one of those blocks in the high 20s that you swear you’ve never been down before.
  • On one occasion, my server was a painter who used to bartend at The Odeon, as painters have done for decades.
  • The twist is that my server’s art was also hanging on the walls of Borgo, as was his daughter’s art.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Borgo sits on one of those blocks in the high 20s that you swear you’ve never been down before. The restaurant opened in 2024 but feels like it’s been there forever, a place with a natural hum and not an ounce of perspiration. Its clientele is specific but unpredictable; when I went there this summer for lunch with a movie producer, we spotted a powerful name-brand media executive, an architectural bigwig who designs the homes of billionaires, and a two-time Academy Award–winning actor. A few nights later, I sat near Walter Isaacson, who’s a regular. And don’t just take it from Elon Musk’s biographer. Matthew Schneier, the chief restaurant critic at Latest York magazine, recently named Borgo the city’s best all-around restaurant.

On one occasion, my server was a painter who used to bartend at The Odeon, as painters have done for decades. He met Ross Bleckner there, and David Salle. He used to have a massive loft studio in Williamsburg, but as rents went up, he moved deeper into Brooklyn, to Fort Greene, where he built a studio in his basement.

The twist is that my server’s art was also hanging on the walls of Borgo, as was his daughter’s art. That’s because he was Andrew Tarlow—the painter and restaurateur who kick-started the Brooklyn aesthetic with his restaurant Diner and, yes, also owns Borgo.

After launching that instant hit in an old, reclaimed diner, Tarlow opened five more era-defining Brooklyn spots before finally venturing into Manhattan with Borgo. All along, he’s still been the artist who got a job at The Odeon so that he could meet his heroes. He’s still painting away in his brownstone, doodling on notepads during concept meetings. He’s had shows recently at galleries such as Tiwa Select; he’s loosely associated with the Galerie Sardine extended universe; and he’s someone whose work I’ve been told about for years by those in the know.

As they put it, Tarlow is an emerging artist who happens to own the best all-around restaurant in Manhattan, as well as a bunch of other successful spots in Brooklyn.

Industry observers note that “I realized, opening Borgo, that I really loved working in restaurants—and not that I had forgotten, but I hadn’t actually worked services in a while until I opened,” Tarlow told me during a studio visit. “And then, in a similar way, I think—I love making paintings. I actually will paint forever, no matter what happens.”.

The studio had dozens of unstretched canvases heaped on the ground, some still rolled up, and others hanging via a pin on the studio wall. They highlighted figures grappling with pain in fierce color-blocked fields, automatic-painting abstractions, faces fading into other faces. One painting was a portrait of the artist Joe Bradley, a friend.

Sources indicate that the studio is in the basement of the Fort Greene brownstone where Tarlow has lived for two decades with his wife, Kate Huling, raising four kids in a kind of neo-boho paradise. There were no studio assistants, no art handlers, no frames, no boxes, no packaging—just the artist and the work.

Industry observers note that “It was kind of just as chaotic as everything else there, but in the most perfect warm embrace of a way. I saw the pure energy that he put into his paintings and the stories that they told,” says Alex Tieghi-Walker, the founder of Tiwa Select, calling from London. “So many artists could be quite—rightfully so, but quite precious with their works. And I love that Andrew was just like, ‘Oh, pull out the ones you’re taking and just take them in an Uber home.’”.

Tarlow grabbed at a canvas bare-handed, one with a bit of a conceptual bent, and put it up on an easel.

“I’ve had this up on the wall for a while now, and I just continued to look at it because I’m happy with it. I’m also a little unsettled—I mean, I’m showing you the inside of my drawers. I’m also a little unsettled by how far it’s gone abstract-wise.”.

Sources indicate that he told me he couldn’t really do his other job, the restaurant job, without painting at odd hours. They’re totally separate, but complementary in a cosmic way.

Industry observers note that “What are the processes? Like you said, for some people, it’s nine to five. Then you listen to the news, smoke a cigarette, drink coffee. It’s either working or it’s not. The door either opens or it’s not,” Tarlow said, gesturing around to his studio. “But I’m going to go here every day, and I’m going to push some paint on canvas.”.

It has been revealed that diner opened in 1999, a few years after Tarlow moved to the desolate southern tip of Broadway in Williamsburg—where the crumbling street dead-ends into the East River. While looking for a cheap studio space, he found a 6,000-square-foot loft across the street from an abandoned diner from the 1920s. The loft’s landlord bought the diner, and in 1999, Tarlow opened Diner with then partner Mark Firth—and watched as it was patronized by only the artists across the street.

“You could stand outside the restaurant in those days and not see a single person walk by,” he told Bon Appetit in 2010.

Tarlow kept expanding. He opened Marlow & Sons, and then the butcher shop and specialty food store Marlow & Daughters. He founded a bakery, She Wolf, and a literary magazine, Diner Journal. He operated the restaurant at the Wythe Hotel, but only for a few years. Instead of doing the easy thing, Vegas-ifying Diner in some fresh development on the Williamsburg waterfront, he got even weirder, opening a nautical bar called Achilles Heel in a far-out corner of Greenpoint.

A dealer with a gallery in Tribeca was the first, but far from the last, to tell me I had to check out Tarlow’s paintings. After an introduction was brokered, Tarlow invited me to lunch at Borgo this past summer. The restaurant has many fantastic pork-laden dishes, but we ate almost entirely vegetables, as well as one very elegant, simple piece of fish. A summer lunch. We fell into an easy patter, talking about exhibitions, other artists—but mostly his painting practice. He’d been working on Long Island, not on the East End but in the middle. He’d had a few shows. There was discussion of representation. He spoke about all this with an unpracticed earnestness and complete confidence. He sounded like a very prominent emerging artist, which, at 56, he is.

“I don’t know if it’s just age or time, or I was too much of a young person, or a young mind, but I’ve been more secure with my ability to hold all these things in the same time,” he told me back in the studio. “I can go work tonight in the restaurant and feel perfectly confident in that work, and I can show you this work and feel perfectly confident in this work. Whereas, I think, as a young person, I felt like, Am I fake?”.

Sometimes it’s not the enfant terrible who breaks out—it’s the working parent, the person with a desk job, the successful entrepreneur who back-ends into revolutionary art making. Think William Carlos Williams writing “The Red Wheelbarrow” while working as a doctor in Rutherford, Latest Jersey. Or Ruth Asawa making art in her kitchen while raising six children in San Francisco. Or Jeff Koons working on Wall Street in order to earn money to make his sculptures. Having a demanding job actually granted them the freedom to be artists. Tarlow started drawing during restaurant concept meetings.

Sometimes Tarlow hangs his own paintings upstairs in his brownstone’s salon room, or at his house on Long Island, to see what they look like in the wild. The paintings have a confident thrust to them, with the colors bold-blocked in a way that reminds me of Albert Oehlen, drawing from Roman and Greek mythology in Twombly-esque riffs: visages multiplying and fading like a Kippenberger-ian pomo ride into the ether. Sure, any painter who’s spent time in Europe since the 1990s has wanted to be Martin Kippenberger. But Tarlow has an actual connection to him: Like Tarlow, Kippenberger was a lover of Italian food and good wine, and he made art to hang in restaurants. And like Tarlow, Kippenberger was a restaurant owner, balancing his studio practice with running Capri, a Venice, California, spot in which he invested after moving to Los Angeles in 1989. According to those present at the time, Kippenberger became a part-owner of the place because, as the artist put it, “You can’t get a decent Bolognese in Los Angeles.”.

As a bartender at The Odeon, Tarlow maintained a working painting studio but found it hard to produce art. After opening Diner, he skipped painting sessions in favor of opening businesses and starting a family. Once that duality settled, he started drawing on the move, carrying sketchbooks and working through potential paintings. Eventually, once the kids got old enough, he built out a studio in a nook of his 19th-century basement.

Sources indicate that “I really started painting back downstairs. Let’s just say, after dinner, it was 8 p.m. and they were watching Nemo. No one actually needs me, they’re totally happy. My wife’s up there, everyone’s laughing, giggling with little fish,” he mentioned. “And I can just walk down here and do my thing. Having it in my house for sure is the only way I could do this amount of work, and for sure even get to this place. Because I do think you have to do a certain amount of work to get to this place unless you’re just a born prodigy. But when you think about the genius of Picasso or whomever, he made a million fucking paintings.”.

Tarlow didn’t really show anyone his work for a long time.

“I met Andrew socially. I knew his restaurants way before I knew Andrew. And one day he was like, ‘Come and see my studio,’” Tieghi-Walker tells me. “It did not surprise me at all that he had an art studio in his basement and that these were the types of works he was creating.”.

It has been revealed that the show at Tiwa Select was on view right as Tarlow was getting ready to open Borgo. There was a certain amount of unconscious transference, Tarlow told me. For the Tiwa dinner, instead of creating name placards, the artist hand-sketched an artwork of each guest’s name on the paper tablecloth. Now, when a regular makes a reservation at Borgo, Tarlow will elegantly sketch out their name on the paper tablecloth.

Sources indicate that the showcasing of his art at Borgo marks the first time Tarlow has put his own work on the premises of his own restaurant. Tarlow doesn’t exactly promote this. When I asked about it, he told me that only one of his own works was up at the moment, then changed the subject. Alex Levy, the media strategist and theater producer, has been a regular at Borgo since it opened. “Borgo is the grown-up Platonic ideal of what a restaurant can be,” he mentioned. After several visits, Levy, who also collects a bit of contemporary art, noticed what was on the walls.

In a recent development, “I complimented one of the paintings, and Andrew said, ‘It’s by my daughter.’ And then he pointed to another one and said, ‘That’s by me,’” Levy indicates. “I had no idea that there’s this whole other part of him.”.

Like Tarlow, Levy balances two seemingly divergent but strangely complementary careers—as a speechwriter on one hand, a Tony Award winner on the other—and Tarlow invited him to see his studio on Long Island. Levy bought a painting immediately. Seeing the studio, Levy states, helped him realize, to some extent, what the special sauce is behind a place like Borgo. It’s for incredibly confident, hyperproductive creative types, run by an artist who has complete faith in his ability to work.

And for Tarlow, the focus and passion in one arena lead right into the passion for the other.

“I’m also being very present for your needs in the same way as I’m trying to be very present with these paintings,” he said. “They’re not separate boats. When the restaurant’s working, I feel creative inside of it.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that shortly it debuted back in 2009, Ryan Murphy's campy musical comedy Glee became a sensation. The series (which is streaming with a Hulu subscription) broke barriers in regards to LGBTQ+ representation, and also featured plenty of memorable musical numbers. The show has also been associated with a number of tragedies, with three main cast members having died, starting with Cory Monteith's death back in 2013. There's been chatter online about the "Glee curse" and now Tina actress Jenna Ushkowitz has issued a heartfelt response about that discourse.

Monteith's death broke the heart of fans and his coworkers alike, with the cast quickly putting together a tribute episode in the midst of their grief. Since then there's been more tragedies with this talented ensemble, such as Naya Rivera's death in 2020. While appearing on the podcast We Need To Talk with Paul C. Brunson, Ushkowitz shared her emotional reaction to folks insensitively talking about the Glee curse.

Industry observers note that my response to the Glee curse, as it’s always been, is we are human. And to hear that people see this as a collective curse that’s like, ‘Who’s next?’ is so unkind. And it shows the way in which we are able to just sit behind our computers and type off whatever we think we’re feeling in that moment without really connecting to what’s behind it and who’s on the other side.

Talk about honesty. While folks online might be talking about the show's curse with levity, the experience of those who actually worked on Glee is another one entirely. Real people died, not characters, which has been a source for quite a bit of pain by the rest of the cast. Those feelings remain to this day, case in point being Harry Shum Jr. honoring Naya Rivera this season on Dancing with the Stars.

In addition to the death of Rivera and Monteith, Puck actor Mark Salling committed suicide back in 2018 before going to prison for possession of child sexual abuse imagery. What's more, an entire docuseries called The Price of Glee was released in 2023 examining the "curse." In the same podcast, Jenna Ushkowitz spoke more about the pain and grief that the cast has dealt with, offering:.

We lost friends. People grieve those people. This is not something that’s, like, ‘Who’s next? This is a game.’ It’s not.

Industry observers note that the internet can be a cruel place, and the discourse about the Glee curse has clearly been painful for the cast. The tragic loss of their coworkers is hard enough, but the light-hearted chatter about these deaths has clearly created more pain for the members of the William McKinley High School Glee Club. Hopefully Ushkowitz's comments will circulate online, and help to quiet that type of talk.

It has been revealed that glee is streaming in its entirety over on Hulu, while fans patiently wait for news about Ryan Murphy's potential reboot. Our thoughts continue to be with the cast as they process their grief.

Lords of the Fallen 2 delayed to April 2027, exact release date coming next month

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lords of the Fallen 2 will now launch in April 2027, and we'll find out exactly when next month.
  • In a recent development, the news came via a short post on X from CI Games founder and CEO Marek Tyminski.
  • Recent findings suggest that that means the Soulslike sequel has slipped again.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lords of the Fallen 2 will now launch in April 2027, and we'll find out exactly when next month.

In a recent development, the news came via a short post on X from CI Games founder and CEO Marek Tyminski. "Lords of the Fallen II: April 2027," he wrote. "Exact date in December.".

Recent findings suggest that that means the Soulslike sequel has slipped again. Back in June, CI Games pushed Lords of the Fallen 2 into a Q1 2027 release window, saying the extra time would let the team refine the game and keep it clear of "a highly competitive holiday period". That was a delay in itself, as when CI Games and Epic ended the game's PC exclusivity deal in May, it was still targeting a 2026 release.

Sources indicate that last month, CI Games secured a €28.6 million (around $32 million) loan to complete production and release Lords of the Fallen 2, as well as refinance its existing bank debt, according to a stock exchange filing. The loan matures on 31st August 2027, and, as reported at the time, CI Games will self-publish the game and expects to repay the loan through its sales.

Industry observers note that lords of the Fallen II: April 2027. Exact date in December. pic.twitter.com/yYaevDqaxe.

Lords of the Fallen 2 is coming to PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store.

Following its announcement in 2025 and a look at gameplay during that year's The Game Awards, Lords of the Fallen 2 - which is technically the series' third game if we don't ignore the fact it was rebooted - had been steadily marching towards an unspecified 2026 launch. On PC, the plan was for it to be an Epic Games Store exclusive, but that's no longer happening after we learned CI Games - developer and sole owner of the IP - is now free from the multi-year exclusivity deal with Epic Games.

The sequel has also been at the centre of heated conversations following CI Games founder and CEO Marek Tyminski's comments regarding "political correctness" and "real player feedback". The studio also raised eyebrows recently by announcing more revealing armour sets for female characters in Lords of the Fallen 2, for instance, compared to its previous project.

Eurogamer gave the rebooted Lords of the Fallen two stars, calling it "a perfectly acceptable Soulslike that's often fun to play and offers the same satisfaction at overcoming adversity", but one let down by "Soulslike clichés and performance woes".

Infamous GTA 6 Leaker Cyberleek resurfaced last week, threatening to release a crucial file for the Xbox build of GTA 6 that could be used to create an unofficial PC port of the game. The hacker originally promised to publicly drop the .exe file for this version of the game depending on whether their memecoin hit a certain market cap, and has been taunting publisher Take-Two Interactive for failing to prevent the game files from leaking online. "Months of takedowns, subpoenas, and wallet-tracing later, the hunt is still on and the uploads keep arriving," Cyberleek wrote in a now-removed post on Reddit, insisting they were "fighting anti-consumerism" in the video games industry with their actions and using crypto funds to work on a new project. "There is no other way to move funds without names," Cyberleek added. "And this work requires no names." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i7l7Lu69V_c As pointed out online, Cyberleek has already cashed out on their memecoin in August and again in October, raking in hundreds of thousands of US dollars. So far, it looks like modders are already making modest headway with the full Xbox build of GTA 6, as the Project Leonida Discord server (via Eurogamer) has footage of the game booting up on PC. That's as far as it gets (for now), as that start-up process is met with a black screen shortly afterward. Modders and homebrew enthusiasts are reportedly using Claude AI to reverse-engineer the game on that platform, and the group is confident that a playable build will be ready within a week. Rockstar has yet to officially announce a PC port of GTA 6, but rumors suggest it could be out in early 2027. This would be a very short gap between console and PC releases for a Rockstar-developed game, as the studio's console-first projects usually spend many months in incubation before heading to PC. The threat of a homebrewed PC port, however, could pressure the developer to release GTA 6 on PC sooner rather than later. Meanwhile, GTA 6 has done phenomenally well on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S since it rolled out last week. The game kicked off with 32.5 million copies sold on its first day, and just a few days later, that number reportedly rose to 44.9 million. PS5 sales have dominated, and Sony notes GTA 6 was the biggest launch in PlayStation history.

Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1155 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI.
  • Sources indicate that GTA 6 is absurdly large.
  • Recent findings suggest that alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI. You’ve preloaded the game on your console, you’ve taken the next month off work, and you’ve locked your phone in a Faraday cage and set it adrift at sea. You’re prepared to lock in, and you haven’t forgotten a thing…right? Well, just to make sure, here are the most vital tips to optimize your setup before you fire up the most anticipated game of the decade.

Sources indicate that GTA 6 is absurdly large. According to Rockstar, you’ll need up to 212GB of storage space. For high-end consoles like the PS5 Pro, that’s more than 10% of the available storage space, and close to half the space on the more budget-conscious Xbox Series S. There’s a good chance you’ll have to delete something to make room.

Recent findings suggest that alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it). External SSDs are probably the cheapest route, though you’ll want to make sure to use a high-speed USB cable to connect it. It’s even worth shopping around for alternate models of SSD. For example, at the time of writing, the popular 2TB WD_BLACK external drive was close to $200, but the exact same drive in pink was $132.

Sources indicate that you can also directly upgrade the storage of your console with expansion drives. The Xbox Series X|S supports proprietary expansion cards, while the PS5 and PS5 Pro can accept most M.2 internal SSDs. These will generally be faster, since they plug directly into the console via higher-speed connections than a drive hooked up via USB.

Recent findings suggest that let’s face it: Half the fun of any sandbox game is the weird, unique stuff that happens to only you. So you’re probably going to be hitting that “record recent gameplay” button more often than usual. While you’re cleaning up your storage space (or adding more), make sure to account for all the video clips you might want to save.

File size of video clips depends on a lot of factors, but 4K recordings can generally take up to 0.5GB per minute of footage. You can cut that down by saving footage in 1080p instead, but either way you’ll want to leave a little extra space.

Sources indicate that game footage is also a pretty good place to look if you need to make room on your console and don’t want to delete any games. Be honest with yourself: You don’t need all those clips from Horizon Forbidden West you saved four years ago. Dive into the settings on your console and find the biggest media files you forgot you even had on there.

According to Rockstar, GTA 6 will be targeting 30fps across consoles at launch, which is pretty low as modern AAA games go. Part of the reason for that is all the processing power going to rendering a complex environment, but it also means you won’t need a fancy high frame rate TV or monitor any time soon to get the most out of it. Still, it couldn’t hurt to check a few settings on your display.

In a recent development, first, make sure you’re using a higher refresh rate than 30Hz. While the game is targeting 30fps, it is technically capable of more, so if your console can keep up, you don’t want to accidentally bottleneck your frames. This setting will vary by device, so check the manual that came with your screen.

It has been revealed that also, make sure you have HDR enabled on your hardware. There’s a good chance this is already turned on for your TV, but sometimes other devices can switch display modes if they only support SDR. The game will help you calibrate your HDR settings for GTA 6 specifically when you launch it, but only if it detects HDR compatibility in the first place.

It has been revealed that if you’re planning to buy a console specifically for GTA 6, this might be one of those rare instances where a PS5 Pro really is worth the upgrade. According to Rockstar, certain features like ray-traced shadows will only be available on the Pro version of Sony’s console.

More importantly, the PS5 Pro version supports PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (or PSSR), which upscales lower-resolution images to get better detail and higher frame rates out of the same hardware. Given that GTA 6 is already starting at a meager target of 30fps on most consoles, anything that can give your frame rate a boost is probably going to feel like a welcome improvement over the baseline.

Recent findings suggest that I’ll tell you a secret as someone who’s spent a lot of time testing different game controllers: Most of the time, you really don’t need an expensive “elite” controller. Most of the time. I don’t buy into the idea that a taller control stick is going to make you an esports athlete. It can be nice to have, but it’s not a game changer. What does matter is customizing your controls, especially for long gaming sessions.

The DualSense Edge wireless controller is a favorite of mine, mainly because of the rear paddles and adjustable triggers. The former lets you map any button to a rear lever that you can access with your fingers underneath the controller, which can often ease some of the wrist strain of awkward button combos. And the adjustable triggers let you activate the buttons with less motion, again reducing repetitive stress.

According to recent reports, the Xbox Elite Series 2 controller has similar features for the Xbox, as well as custom caps for the D-pad. Both consoles’ versions of pro controllers are more expensive than the standard ones, but if you’re planning to game for many hours, it can be worth it to get a controller that’s more comfortable for you.

It has been revealed that if you have an Xbox One, you don’t necessarily have to upgrade your console to play GTA 6, but you might want to take a look at your network. GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on day one, and you’ll be able to stream the game to an Xbox One console (as long as you purchase Cloud playtime as well or get some with your Game Pass subscription). This is the only way to play on a console older than the current generation, so if you don’t want to shell out for new hardware, this might be your best bet.

Xbox recommends a minimum of a 20Mbps connection to run cloud gaming, but more is obviously better. If you can connect your console to a wired Ethernet connection, that would be better and provide more stability. If you can’t connect a cable, then at least make sure you’re well within range of your wifi router, and try to limit any other bandwidth-hogging applications on the network while you’re playing.

Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto 6 has managed to get its claws into just about everyone. Honestly, I can't go anywhere without hearing something from the soundtrack or someone talking about how much fun it is to joyride around Leonida. And now it's even infested the sports I watch.

To keep non-Formula One fans up to speed, it was the Las Vegas Grand Prix over the weekend, one of the newer circuits on the calendar. Third place went to Oscar Piastri. In second place was his McLaren teammate and previous world champion for 2025, Lando Norris. And first place went to four-time F1 world champion Max Verstappen, not exactly very surprising given his history with the track. But it is a little more impressive when you take into account that Verstappen has also put 40 hours into GTA 6, much of which would have been before the race.

Industry observers note that "I played a lot in the evening and in the morning in Vegas," he notes in a stream (via IGN), correcting the idea that he actually spent the plane ride home playing GTA 6 instead of spending time doing so around the race. "I mean I can't go out anyways [in the evening and morning], and walk around.".

Verstappen did, however, explain that the aspect that GTA 6 has likely affected the most is his ability to play Minecraft, which he had planned to stream later this week: "I'm so bad when I play too many games at the same time. I can't, I just can't.".

GTA 6 to Minecraft is certainly a jump, but you can't really blame anyone for trying to maximise their time in Leonida right now. I'll also take any chance to spend every free moment playing the game, the only difference being that instead of subsequently competing in an F1 race and winning it, I spend the next day of work acting like a zombie—a poorly functioning one at that. I suppose people are just built differently, or at least that's what I'll tell myself while I'm on my third cup of coffee in three hours.

Nvidia has lost more than $2 trillion in market cap since early October, but on Thursday, Anthropic’s IPO minted a class of new billionaires. It’s whiplash. It’s the most expensive work sold at auction this year, and easily among the top 10 priciest things to ever be publicly auctioned. It’s a bit insane to say this, especially about a single canvas that sold for more than the total value of the art set to be on offer at Art Basel Miami Beach next month, but that price feels a bit like a…disappointment? The on-request estimate for the work was $180 million, and the hammer price fell well short of that, at $165 million. Bidding in the room was thin, and the lot was guaranteed by Sotheby’s. Though it’s unclear where the exact guarantee price landed, it was probably around the estimate.

It has been revealed that honestly, it’s a relief to the house and the seller—the family of the Argentinian collectors Carlos Pedro Blaquier and Nelly Arrieta de Blaquier—that this painting sold at all. A Jewish collector bought the work in 1909 from a Paris gallery. His heirs claimed, just days before the auction, that the work was later sold under duress due to Nazi persecution, entitling them to receive restitution. The parties came together over an eleventh hour deal, terms undisclosed, to allow the sale to go through.

Sources indicate that so who bought it? The winning bidder in the room was William Acquavella, the patriarch of one of Upcoming York’s great art-dealing families, who has an august gallery on the Upper East Side. It’s unclear for whom he bought it. In the past he’s been known to broker art deals on behalf of former Las Vegas casino tycoon Steve Wynn. In 2013, Acquavella was the winning bidder on a Francis Bacon tryptic for $142 million—that time on behalf of Wynn’s ex-wife, the late Elaine Wynn. (The piece is presently on view at LACMA, where Elaine Wynn was a co-chair of the board.) Steve Wynn has been more of a seller than a buyer recently, so the jury’s still out on whom Acquavella was on the phone with Wednesday.

Recent findings suggest that the $190 million price tag is an almost exact match for the amount someone else paid for another Van Gogh from the Blaquier-Arrieta family. Reports say that, in 2025, Christie’s conducted a private sale where Le Zouave, a Van Gogh portrait of a soldier, sold for $190 million. While there’s no indication that the most recent buyer was someone connected to the AI gold rush, it’s surely indicative of the times that a Van Gogh has sold for 9 figures right around the moment that the seven cofounders of Anthropic have become worth about $20 billion—and around 600 Anthropic employees have become worth more than $100 million. When reached for comment through a rep, Acquavella didn’t get back to me.

Sources indicate that — As I walked into Sotheby’s Monday for the first sales of the week, there were clients going downstairs to get their tables at Marcel, where diners can bid tableside while cocktails are served from a bar cart. Other clients went to a sumptuous overflow room with an open bar and a large spread of Marcel goodies. Those lucky enough to snag seats moseyed up to the sales room, where telecom billionaire Patrick Drahi, the owner of Sotheby’s, was standing in the back, near CEO Charles Stewart.

It has been revealed that the 6 p.m. start time meant some collectors were still trickling in when Jackie Wachter snagged a Gerhard Richter work for a hammer price of $5 million. In the back of the room, white-jacketed waiters wheeled around with flutes of Champagne for those standing in the back. The writer Anthony Haden-Guest, a longtime Vanity Fair scribe whose book True Colors gave this column its name, walked in and took a seat in the back. One woman started taking selfies. As the contemporary sale got underway, Leonardo DiCaprio and his girlfriend, Vittoria Ceretti, walked down from the skybox and watched as an Agnes Martin hammered at $9.2 million. DiCaprio, a very serious collector, didn’t appear to be bidding, but no matter; he was still there at Sotheby’s. Auction week had officially begun.

It has been revealed that — Over at Christie’s, the house sold a Georgia O’Keeffe that had been on view in an apartment in my neighborhood for more than 60 years. Suffice to say, there aren’t many expensive works of art that get discovered in apartments in the vicinity of Tompkins Square Park. I had to savor the lot’s beautifully poetic provenance, a phrasing that I don’t believe has ever been printed in an auction catalog previously: “Property from an East Village Private Collection.” It sold for $4.9 million.

— The week’s hottest lot? Maybe a sculpture of a dog by Jeff Koons, Bob-Tail, that was first on view at the artist’s still-controversial “Made in Heaven” show. Estimated to sell for an ambitious high estimate of $3.5 million, it hammered at $9 million, or $9.7 million with fees. Former auction chairman Frances Outred mentioned the sculpture was consigned by a college friend of his who bought it from Anthony d’Offay for a five-figure sum in 1995, “when the art market was in the doldrums and the Jeff Koons market was at its nadir.”.

It wasn’t exactly a tough sell to get the works at the dinner—Bradley is married to Galerie Sardine founder Valentina Akerman. The always exquisite Ignacio Mattos whipped up some Estela-level pinchos ahead of serving an unctuously rich rice-and-chicken dish.

For context: The cathedral would take up nearly four whole blocks of downtown Marfa, Texas. In addition to Speyer, the honorees included photojournalist Lynsey Addario and musician Lyle Lovett, who was introduced by VF contributing photographer Mark Seliger. The evening raised $1.5 million for Ballroom Marfa.

Sources indicate that — After the auction on Wednesday, the gallery Entrance, a space opened by dealer Louis Shannon on Ludlow Street nearly a decade ago, hosted an opening for the painter Victoire Bourgois. Industry observers note that on a Friday in November, I walk into Gagosian on Madison Avenue for a meeting with Michael Chow, the artist, collector, filmmaker, designer, actor, and founder of the restaurant Mr. Chow. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, if you don't own a PlayStation 5 Pro, the best way to play Grand Theft Auto 6 is reportedly on Xbox Series X.
  • The findings come from the tech experts Digital Foundry, who published a significant report covering all the technical similarities and differences between Sony and Microsoft's consoles.
  • Industry observers note that unsurprisingly, PS5 Pro is in the lead with no competition, as Xbox elected not to release a mid-generation upgrade for the Series console family.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if you don't own a PlayStation 5 Pro, the best way to play Grand Theft Auto 6 is reportedly on Xbox Series X. That's according to latest performance analysis, which demonstrates Microsoft's console is more consistent at maintaining the game's 30fps frame-rate target than the base PS5.

The findings come from the tech experts Digital Foundry, who published a significant report covering all the technical similarities and differences between Sony and Microsoft's consoles.

Industry observers note that unsurprisingly, PS5 Pro is in the lead with no competition, as Xbox elected not to release a mid-generation upgrade for the Series console family. Sony's more powerful console delivers "the definitive console GTA 6 experience," according to Digital Foundry. The PS5 Pro has the most stable 30fps performance of all four consoles, and benefits from a sharper presentation at 4K thanks to Sony's PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) image upscaler, which upscales the image from a 1440p base resolution.

It's when comparing the base consoles - Xbox Series X and PS5 - that things get a little more interesting. Both target a 30fps frame-rate and often maintain that target, but certain sections trigger drops. According to the report, those include sequences with busy crowds and fast vehicle traversal. In some cases, the drops can be as low as mid-to-high 20fps.

In a recent development, with that in mind, PS5 has "substantially more frequent" frame-rate drops compared to Series X. The Xbox console is also aided by its support for 120Hz Variable Refresh Rate (VRR), which helps smooth out small dips in the frame-rate.

"Ultimately, Series X is meaningfully better off," Digital Foundry concluded.

Despite the studio's close marketing alignment with PlayStation historically - to the point Xbox can't even say GTA 6 in certain posts about GTA 6 - this is not the first time a Rockstar game has run better or looked better on an Xbox console.

According to recent reports, at Red Dead Redemption 2's launch in 2018, Digital Foundry hailed Xbox One X as the best place to play it, owing to - unsurprisingly - a more stable 30fps frame-rate and sharper visuals. Not much has changed in the past eight years on that front, then.

Recent findings suggest that given all the information we have today, including the lack of 60fps and 40fps modes on PS5 Pro, it's going to be really interesting to see the kind of PC specs required to achieve parity with console visuals at 60fps and beyond. If Rockstar doesn't get there first, modders are already working on porting GTA 6 to PC.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The late Patrick Stewart managed to shoot one last movie before his death, but it was not without difficulty.

The legendary actor died in October from Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia. He was 86.

Stewart’s final movie, Marvel Studios’ highly anticipated Avengers: Doomsday, is set for release on December 18, and directors Anthony and Joe Russo, as well as Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige, recalled how he gave a speech on his final day on set.

“I think it was in the back of all of our heads [that] we may never see him on set again,” Anthony told Entertainment Weekly in an interview published on Tuesday, November 24.

“It was clear that he was struggling with his health, and he worked so hard to deliver a performance and a presence — for us as directors, for his other actors, for the crew,” Anthony continued.

Anthony added, “You could see it wasn’t just the effort of a regular actor showing up and delivering that kind of presence and performance and experience for others, collaboration. It was someone who was really being challenged in a very deep way on a health level, showing up and doing that. For him to have muscled through and delivered the performance that he did in that movie and the experience that he delivered for all of us as collaborators, it made it intensely emotional.”.

Stewart reprises his role as X-Men leader Professor Charles Xavier in the new Avengers movie.

According to Entertainment Weekly, he was offered the chance to reprise his character in both Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars, which is due for release next year, but he decided to only feature in the first film.

Feige told the outlet that Marvel is planning to include a special tribute to Stewart — who first played Professor X in 2000’s X-Men nearly three decades ago — in Avengers: Doomsday.

In a recent development, “We’re long done filming that movie, and he did an amazing job for us,” he told the outlet. “We’re looking now at how we can put something together that honors and respects our friend.”.

Stewart’s spokesperson confirmed his death on October 29.

In a recent development, “He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all,” his rep noted in a statement to Us. “We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace.”.

Check our latest news in Google News.

Check our latest news in Apple News.

Stewart’s widow, Sunny Ozell, paid tribute to the actor in an Instagram statement on November 10.

“The grief continues to come in waves. But I’ve also been experiencing such deep, profound gratitude. We left nothing unsaid,” Ozell, 47, shared. “He knew I loved him, and I know he loved me. Patrick and I truly, authentically saw one another, and we amplified each other’s best qualities.”.

Avengers: Doomsday is in theaters on Friday, December 18.

As part of its 25th anniversary celebrations, Microsoft also teased a few more details about Project Helix, calling it specifically "a console" that plays games from your PC, not "a PC that can also play console games." 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AIGrand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Recomp.

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 is the closest thing we’ve had to a modern monoculture moment in video games in a long time, but you can only play it if you own a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S. If you lack either of those consoles and find the increasingly high prices to be off-putting, you might feel a little left out, especially as Rockstar refuses to talk about whatever intends it has for an inevitable PC release. That feeling of missing out is likely a substantial part of the motivation driving people to tug at Claudeâs apron to get GTA 6 ported to PC ASAP, before any official port is confirmed.

Sources indicate that like other recent recompilations of games, both those created by AI and those that werenât, efforts to port GTA VI to PC were supposed to take the code of the console game and make it playable on a different platform than originally intended. This, in theory, skirts legal issues by requiring a copy of the game already in storage to fill in everything that is owned by Rockstar and Take-Twoâlike assets, voice acting, and so forth. This legal gray area was further complicated this week when Cyberleek, the rogue person or group that released numerous leaks of GTA 6 beginning in August, released the Xbox Series X executable online, bypassing the need for any recompilation project to have a legitimate copy of the game. That release, combined with ubiquitously available AI coding tools and a lot of motivated teenagers, served as a starting pistol for a major effort to get the port done before the end of the year.

Recent findings suggest that on PortWatch VI, a website created to track the progress of community efforts to port GTA 6, a counter at the top proudly counts up the time since the executable was released. The site uses progress bars to show how far along each recompilation is getting, with pinned posts celebrating how far it has come in a short period of time. Currently the recomp is described as playable at sub-5 frames per second.

For whatever reason, a lot of these vibe coders are streaming their attempts to have Anthropicâs Claude port the game to PC for them. While Twitch pretty explicitly does not allow this, right-wing corollaries like Kick and Rumble do with little to no moderation. Bluesky account amithero.bot posted a thread on the site about watching one of these attempts in which the person behind it was largely just tell Claude or Google Antigravity to press A at the title screen and to code faster.

According to recent reports, the thing about publicly streaming these things, though, is that Take-Two’s lawyers are also watching them. Project Leonida, the biggest community built around porting GTA 6 to PC, has had its Discord taken down following a request from Rockstar and Take-Two. The 15-year-old creator of the project posted on X to say that they’re stepping back to focus on schoolwork and deleted many of their posts shortly thereafter, though their replies confirm that Discord banned their account for two years.

https://x.com/ItsNotRexed/status/2125003917880643828.

A remaining post from 12 hours ago advises followers to ignore their other posts and to watch for something big coming soon. It’s possible that Project Leonidaâs creator has not taken the lesson to heart on this one.

Take-Two also requested that software and coding documentation site GitHub remove the main repository for Project Leonida and all its forks. A DMCA notice posted by GitHub explains that, since the network that contained the infringing content was so large, GitHub applied the takedown notice to all 3,007 repositories.

Recent findings suggest that it’s unclear how Take-Two and Rockstar blueprint to proceed against the other recompilation projects in the works or if this will just be an ongoing game of whack-a-mole. A website showing Rockstar lawyers which projects are the closest to completion is undoubtedly helpful for pushing some back down, but itâs the projects that arenât publicly sharing their progress that are the most likely to make it across the finish line. If that happens, there may be no way to really keep a lid on this.

Maybe Rockstar and Take-Two can take some comfort in how unlikely it is that all that many people will be trawling GitHub repositories or even torrent sites to find and run a recompilation, even one that presumably makes things very easy for them. Weighed against what GTA 6 has already sold and what it’s likely to still sell on PC, the number of people that choose to experience the game through a vibe-coded port from the Xbox Series X to the PC is likely not particularly significant. Still, it’s a chilling warning of what AI tools are threatening to do to the video game industry at large.

According to recent reports, black Friday is usually a great time to grab a fresh e-reader, but the ongoing RAM crisis has made that a question mark this year: Amazon recently raised the prices of all its Kindles by around $50 and refreshed the entire lineup, which means your odds of grabbing one at a big discount are low. But you aren't totally out of luck: If you haven't noticed, micro-e-readers—I'm talking credit card-sized, with screens that measure around four inches—are all the rage in 2026, and right now, you can pick up one of them for around $55.

According to recent reports, if you too can see the appeal of carrying all of your books with you on a device so small you'll forget it's even in your pocket, it's a great time to jump in: The recently released Xteink X4 Classic is right now 38% off for Black Friday, bringing it down to $54.87, a record-low price. Meanwhile, the smaller X3 is $55.72, or 19% off. Both are available in either "mist grey" or "space black." The discounts should last through the end of Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

Xteink is a Chinese startup that shook up the e-reading world last year with the launch of the X4, a super bare-bones device that made up for its lack of features and usability with a cheap sub-$70 price point. Since then, a huge online community of fans has formed, sharing tips on Reddit and even coming together to crowdsource an alternate operating system that fixed a lot of early problems. Xteink quickly followed up the X4 with a slate of other devices, including the 3.7-inch X3 and the X4 Pro, which adds a front light and touchscreen (at the cost of screen clarity and two physical buttons).

According to recent reports, the X4 Classic and the X3 improve on the original X4 with quality-of-life upgrades like a larger battery, relocated page-turn buttons, a real-time clock, and a tilt-to-turn-page feature. They're also lighter and thinner than the X4, though there is a trade-off involved: They drop the USB-C charging port in favor of magnetic pogo pins that require a separate adapter (included).

Sources indicate that these upgrades also increased the cost: The X4 Classic typically retails for $89, $20 more than the discontinued X4 and only $10 less than the X4 Pro, while the X3 launched at $79. But right now, the X4 Classic is just under $55, or around 38% off, and the X3 is about a dollar more. Either is a great option for those who prioritize crisp, readable text above the conveniences of a built-in light or touchscreen, as those add extra layers between the inner screen and outer glass. It's also crucial to understand what you're getting into: These devices support only e-books without Digital Rights Management (DRM), which means you can't use it to read your existing library of Kindle books. On the plus side, there's no longer a need to worry about flashing new firmware if you don't want to, as the native version has been totally overhauled and is now one of your best options (though the new firmware, called "Licorice," isn't available on the X3 quite yet).

Industry observers note that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

Spoilers for Season 3, Episode 7 of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power are ahead! You can stream the entire third season with an Amazon Prime subscription now.

Sauron is one of the most legendary villains, and in Season 3 of The Rings of Power, we’ve really gotten to see him ascend to that level as he crafts the One Ring. In the seventh episode of the season airing on the 2026 TV schedule, he finally forged the terrifying piece of jewelry that causes a whole lot of problems in Middle-earth. While it was an epic moment to watch on TV, it turns out the story behind filming it is hilarious.

Recent findings suggest that knowing how much Charlie Vickers cares about Sauron and telling this story, I knew forging the One Ring would be a massive moment for him behind the scenes. It’s also just objectively a huge moment in the season both from a lore perspective and a logistics perspective, seeing as the sequence from when he starts to forge the ring to the moment he puts it on is well over ten minutes long. When I asked Vickers about filming this, he told me why it was so exciting and rewarding to do:.

It has been revealed that it was amazing. It was twofold because like three seasons and getting to the point, like the seminal moment, was – that felt like a huge deal. But also getting to the end of that sequence, right? Because it's a long sequence when you watch it. It was a long sequence to film.

I can only imagine how long it took. Plus, it must have been exhausting, considering he was hammering the ring for quite some time. To that point, Vickers told me that while Sauron’s reward was the ring, his reward as an actor was simply getting to the end of the scene, as he said:.

In a recent development, as Charlie, I also had a reward. My reward at the end of it was I get to hold the ring and lift up the ring, and finally say the ring poem. Because before that, it was a lot of hammering and a lot of broken hammers and blistering.

In a recent development, alright, here’s where things get funny. As the Sauron actor was telling me this story, he went on a small tangent about the gloves he was wearing. It turns out he busted through one of them while filming all of this. However, if you want to know why, he hilariously can’t give you that answer:.

And there was one bit where, you know, when I'm like smashing the thing, oh, and the lava is raining down on me, and I have to go, ‘Ah! My hand's really hot,’ and I take off my gloves. I smashed my hand through the end of the glove. Like I just busted the glove open because, um, I don't know why that happens, but it was exhausting. So it was incredible.

I’d like to point out, and you can see this in the video above, that when Charlie Vickers remarked he didn’t know why he busted his glove open, Jamie Campbell Bower, who plays Celeborn and was sitting right next to him, burst out laughing. It really was hilarious, too. That’s because here we have arguably one of the most intense and anticipated moments in Rings of Power history, and the star of it – the man who plays Sauron – recalling said story in a very casual, chill and funny way.

Plus, the plot twist at the end of him breaking the glove and having no idea how he did it really was the nail in the coffin that got both me and the Celeborn actor giggling during the interview.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

It has been revealed that anyway, silliness aside, this sequence is epic in Rings of Power. Vickers is so commanding as Sauron, and watching him forge the One Ring was surreal in a lot of ways. We’ve seen the iconic ring in The Lord of the Rings movies, and the last three seasons of Rings of Power have been building to it. So, to finally watch Sauron bring it into existence was incredible. And honestly, the funny story behind it makes it even better.

Now, considering we know Rings of Power Season 4 is happening, here’s hoping we get more legendary moments like this one and more silly stories behind them.

Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto 6 gets downright weird when you go off the beaten track, and one secret mission will see you travel to the bowels of hell to fight Beezleboss himself, Satan. This detour is worth it because you'll get cool cosmetics and a powerful shotgun, plus a nice little bump to your health. Here's how you can start this Doom-inspired mission in GTA 6. How to go to Hell in GTA 6 You can find this mission in Port Gellhorn, Kelly County, and it's generally recommended that you tackle it once you've gotten your bearings in Chapter 2 of GTA 6. You can access it with either Jason or Lucia, and you'll need to follow these steps to find it: https://youtu.be/Y3tU0mXzto0 Start the mission at night, preferably around midnight. Go to the northern section of Port Gellhorn (as indicated on the maps) and look for the Circles of Hell, a house with an open garage. Inside the garage, you'll find two NPCs rocking out. Press L2 to highlight them and start talking. Select the dialogue options "Having fun?" and "It's good" when prompted. Follow the NPCs into a van that appears shortly afterward, and get inside. After being transported to the camping grounds, press L2 to stare into the campfire. Once you've done all that, you'll be taken to Hell, and you'll have to face off against an army of demons. Don't worry! You'll be equipped with a powerful shotgun, so you can mow down the demons and fight your way to Satan. The Prince of Darkness will occasionally summon reinforcements to defend him, but the denizens of hell are no match for a few well-placed shotgun rounds. Finish off the devils, and you'll wake up at the campsite. For your efforts, you'll be rewarded with the following items and upgrades: Circles of Hell top Upcoming tattoo design Hellspawn Comshot 12 shotgun (collect it next to the throne) Permanent health boost For a closer look at GTA 6's supernatural side, check out how to encounter an unkillable NPC, solve the Bigfoot mystery, and help out some friendly aliens. Capcom's sci-fi dinosaur shooter Exoprimal is shutting down next year

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that sad news dinosaur lovers.
  • Recent findings suggest that in a new post to the official Exoprimal website, it's revealed the game will be shuttered on 29th September 2027, at 8am PDT across all regions.
  • If you do fancy hopping in for a bit to send off Exoprimal in style, you'll still be able to re-download the game after it's taken off stores if you originally downloaded the game in the past.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that sad news dinosaur lovers. Exoprimal - Capcom's third-person sci-fi shooter with a Jurassic twist - will be shutting down next year. With its closure, the game will no longer be playable, even for those who've got it downloaded.

Recent findings suggest that in a new post to the official Exoprimal website, it's revealed the game will be shuttered on 29th September 2027, at 8am PDT across all regions. Until then, all Survival Passes (battle pass equivalents) are no longer available for purchase, with the game and all its DLC stripped from stores on 30th March.

If you do fancy hopping in for a bit to send off Exoprimal in style, you'll still be able to re-download the game after it's taken off stores if you originally downloaded the game in the past. Tragically, the game will no longer be playable at all once shuttered, as there's no offline support. As an always-online game that requires a constant internet connection, it'll be one for the history books, at least in an official capacity.

Exoprimal was an interesting game for certain. A spin on the popular hero shooter, the game blended staples from the genre with some fairly cool twists. For one, the PvE elements were immediately interesting: seeing waves of raptors race towards you and your allies was critical to its appeal. On top of that, the PvPvE elements where two teams would race to complete objectives was pretty neat, thanks in large part to a variety of enjoyable exosuits at your disposal.

It has been revealed that even so, the game never really caught on to the extent that its peers did. Many pointed to the premium price tag paired with in-game microtransactions as a core factor to this, believing it would be hard to convince someone to play the game over something like Overwatch, which was free. Still, it had nearly a million players soon after launch, with Capcom stating it expected the game to be profitable in a financial report following the game's release. Whether or not it actually was remains unclear.

With that in mind, pay some mind to the Exoprimal players who don't have too long left with their game of choice. All the Krieger players out there have my sympathies. All the Vigilant players do not.

#108814. Industry News: How To Play GTA 6 On Your PC Or Phone Via Remote Play On Xbox

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (985 w)

Industry News: How To Play GTA 6 On Your PC Or Phone Via Remote Play On Xbox

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (985 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 can be streamed via Xbox Cloud Gaming, and Microsoft has also now confirmed support for Remote Play on Xbox.
  • Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 can be streamed via Xbox Cloud Gaming, and Microsoft has also now confirmed support for Remote Play on Xbox.
  • Remote Play is an Xbox service that lets you stream games from your Xbox Series X|S to a device you might already have, and it's easy to get working.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 can be streamed via Xbox Cloud Gaming, and Microsoft has also now confirmed support for Remote Play on Xbox. This means you can play GTA 6 on your PC, smartphone, or a device like Xbox Rog Ally. Remote Play is an Xbox service that lets you stream games from your Xbox Series X|S to a device you might already have, and it's easy to get working. From your console, select Settings then Devices & connections then Remote features. From there, check the box for Enable remote features. Xbox Remote Play also has a "test" feature so you can preview the experience in your home environment before going further. From there, you can play GTA 6 from a mobile device by accessing the Xbox Remote Play website, selecting the console you want to connect to, and then the device. To play GTA 6 on your PC or Xbox Rog Ally, owners can open the Xbox app for PC, click on their profile, then select Accessories & Remote Play and then select Remote Play to choose the device to play on. Additionally, people have spotted that GTA 6's store page on the PlayStation Store now mentions that Remote Play is supported and that PlayStation 5 and PlayStation Portal owners can use cloud streaming if they have a Premium membership. Right now, you need a PS5 or Xbox Series X|S to stream GTA 6, but some are dreaming of the day when you can simply stream the game to your PC or phone without any expensive hardware. That day may eventually come for GTA 6, as Take-Two's own CEO has said the rising cost of gaming hardware is not a good thing and that streaming games could be a big business very soon. “If you believe in streaming, and to be clear, we really do, and I’m happy to put a timeline on it. I think we’ll be in commercial streaming mode within three years, and by commercial, I mean low latency," Strauss Zelnick said. "That can 10x the effective installed base. Now, it doesn’t mean we’re going to 10x our revenue–and we wouldn’t project that we would–but because obviously your avid consumers already had access to video game machines. But I do think it creates great opportunity for titles that are broadly desirable, even outside of core markets.” GTA 6 is doing just fine without the potential expanded reach of streaming. After all, the game sold 32.5 million copies before launch and generated close to $4 billion in revenue by day one. Even if GTA 6 doesn't add support for full streaming without a console, the game is expected to expand its reach in a major way in 2027 with an expected PC release. Beyond that, GTA 6 is reportedly going to add an online mode in 2027 as well, and it could be bigger than Fortnite.

#108813. Deborah Nevins—a Legend of Landscape Architecture—Plants With Purpose
