  • Industry observers note that with the upcoming Hunger Games film, it’s Grace’s turn to adopt the trend.
  • In a wide-ranging conversation, Dickson breaks down all the looks that set the Hunger Games fans’ hearts aflame, from Rue’s blue dress to Katniss’ Mockingjay gown, and all the threads that came together for Grace’s most memorable press appearances yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Before the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping press tour began, Mckenna Grace knew she wanted to be method dressed for her appearances. Made a household term by Law Roach and Zendaya, method dressing is when actors wear looks that pay homage to the film or show they’re promoting: See Zendaya’s on-theme looks across red carpets for Dune, Spiderman, and The Odyssey for a slew of examples.

Industry observers note that with the upcoming Hunger Games film, it’s Grace’s turn to adopt the trend. A super fan of the Suzanne Collins book series and their film adaptations, Grace—who plays District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner—took a hand in the styling for her press run, weaving easter eggs into every look. Her stylist, Molly Dickson, was up for the challenge of translating Grace’s deep-cut references into custom and archival looks from Monique Lhuillier, Gucci, Celine and more.

In a wide-ranging conversation, Dickson breaks down all the looks that set the Hunger Games fans’ hearts aflame, from Rue’s blue dress to Katniss’ Mockingjay gown, and all the threads that came together for Grace’s most memorable press appearances yet.

Vanity Fair: How did you get into styling?

Molly Dickson: I went to college in Minnesota and my major was advertising. Two weeks before I graduated, I called my mom and said, "I'm not into this. I don't wanna do advertising." She said, "Well, what do you wanna do?" I told her, "I wanna do fashion. I wanna go to Upcoming York." She said, "No, absolutely not.".

According to recent reports, right after I graduated, I went to LA, this was 2009 during the recession, and no one was hiring. I got an internship at Marie Claire in Newly introduced York, and enrolled back into college to get school credit to intern at Hearst. I worked at Marie Claire as a market assistant for almost two years, and then I left and assisted Leslie Fremar for seven years. That's when I fell in love with celebrity. Then ten years ago, I went off on my own.

What would you say are your aesthetic influences as a stylist?

Recent findings suggest that my personal style relates very similarly to Sadie Sink's style, very effortless. She always wants to be very comfortable and easy, never anything frilly or over the top. Just a simple, beautiful dress, and you let it speak for itself.

Mckenna is a big fan of the original film series, so it’s clear you’re pulling from there as influences when dressing her. Is it a collaborative process when coming to one of these referential looks?

She's obviously a very huge fan of the franchise. We actually started having conversations about this tour in April, which is very early to start having conversations. I could just sense her excitement around it. She started sending me mood boards, and I actually looked back today at the mood board and it was, it was a lot of Katniss Everdeen. It had Joanna on it, and it was filled with these really strong female characters from the franchise.

In a recent development, what she really wanted to hit was Katniss’ wedding gown look and the Mockingjay look with the wings. I was really stumped on how to pull that off without making it overly costumey.

Mckenna kept asking, "What's going on with those?" I knew the vision, but I didn't know how to execute it. I was working with Keke Palmer and the designer Michael Ngo. He was making some cool music costumes for Keke, and I asked, "Michael, could you make this silver piece?" 'Cause I really had no idea how to get it done.

According to recent reports, he stated, “I don't think I can do that. You know what? Just give me a day, let me play around with it." That night, he said, "I figured it out." We got the piece and I thought, "Okay, it needs to be a wedding dress under,” so I reached out to all the bridal houses. I wanted it to be vintage because it would tell a pretty story. Monique [Lhuillier] ended up sending a ton of wedding gowns, and the day before Mckenna came in for the fitting, I actually tried the wedding dresses on myself with the silver piece.

I sent Mckenna five dresses, and the one that she ended up wearing, she stated, "That's it. I don't even need to try anything else. That's the one I'm gonna wear." Then, it was a matter of finding the right event to wear it to because it’s pretty nice, very dramatic.

Recent findings suggest that she was in Paris for the Miu Miu show, and I brought it there because she had the Hunger Games Museum event. It was a whole conversation with her team, like, "Is it the right moment? Is it too much for this event?" Her PR stated, "No, this is the perfect moment. It's the best way to kick off the tour." The response with the Hunger Games fans—I have never seen anything like it before, ever.

What was the experience of having her be such a massive part of the styling process?

According to recent reports, it makes my job so fun because she is so passionate about it and she loves Hunger Games so much, even just finding subtle nods back to the movie. She would say, "I wanna do a ladybug look." Thom Browne did that amazing ladybug dress, I thought, "That's so cool, but it's not really her personal aesthetic." So it’s finding ways to keep it still true to her personal style while maintaining the nods to the film.

It has been revealed that the way you seem to understand Mckenna feels something similar to the connection between Katniss and Cinna in The Hunger Games. When pulling looks for her, what comes into play? How do you make her come through and not be lost in the lore of the stories or the dress?

Mckenna had mentioned that she maybe wanted to do a red or a dark pink feather look because in the books [Maysilee] gets attacked by the red birds which are like flamingos. I'm pulling in all these red feather dresses and on the runway, this one dress looked amazing. Mckenna said, “That's perfect for the flamingo reference.”.

But we put it on her and it was so big, and she's so petite so she was just getting swarmed. I noted, “Let"s not force it.” The goal was for her to feel comfortable in the look rather than just getting each reference.

The public has been really excited about these looks. Are you thinking about the response to the looks when you’re putting them together?

There's been some conversations in a fitting, like, "Oh, the Hunger Games fans are gonna get this." They're gonna see the inspiration, they're gonna understand it.

But I wouldn't say we're choosing a look because ‘Oh, this is gonna go viral to the Hunger Games community.’ Mckenna is a super fan herself so if she's getting excited about the look, everyone else that's a fan of the franchise is gonna get excited about the look.

Mckenna Grace in Betsey Johnson.

Do you feel any pressure to top the last outfit after each premiere?

According to recent reports, yes. I think it was Paris because that wedding dress did get so much press. In that fitting, it felt like, "We gotta keep our game up high." It's been really fun for my team and market assistants because a lot of the girls that work with me are huge fans of the movie. They're not even seeing it as work. They're like, "Oh my God, this is so exciting. Look at this. This looks like this from the movie.".

What was the inspiration to do method dressing for this press run? What do you think is the value?

Mckenna knew back in April, she stated, "I wanna do method for this." I personally did not read the books. I'm a visual person, so I've seen all the movies. Lionsgate was able to let me go with the cast when they first saw the movie because my agent was like, "Molly needs to go to the movie to get inspired before this press tour. She can't do a method dressing press tour without seeing the movie.".

Even as the tour was going on, Mckenna kept sending me upcoming references and quotes from the book and stuff like that.

Industry observers note that what made you take it to the next level? From paying homage to not only characters, but the actual actors from the films like Jennifer Lawrence at the 2011 Oscars to even dressing like set pieces from the film.

In a recent development, that was all Mckenna's vision. On her first mood board, she had a lot of Jennifer Lawrence's red carpet moments because she's such a huge fan of Katniss and Jennifer Lawrence.

With the Rue reference, Mckenna thought that color was just very Hunger Games. It wasn't until she put the dress on, her mom noted, "Wait, this is Rue's dress." So that was just fate. I would love to take credit for that.

Why do you think that this styling has generated so much attention?

In a recent development, I think it’s when you do method dressing for such a massive franchise and you really are passionate about it. The thing is that Mckenna is so excited and passionate about this movie. She has said, “I didn't think that I would love doing fittings so much. I used to hate doing fittings.”.

Mckenna Grace in Elisabetta Franchi.

In a recent development, because every look is so intentionally tied back to Hunger Games and she's such a significant fan, it's literally like playing dress up with her. I think the fans see it, she's so relatable because she's a fan that all these fans think, "Wow, like, she's a fan and she got to do this." She’s the fangirl living out her dream, and the fans are excited for her that she finally gets to do this.

Recent findings suggest that what do you think are the best kinds of projects to implement method dressing with/works best with? What does it work best with?

I think the significant movies that already have a fan base, like Barbie or Wednesday, Being able to pull inspiration from existing books or films makes it so much easier for a stylist rather than a movie that no one's seen before. There's no curiosity or momentum about it because you're starting from scratch, whereas Hunger Games, Barbie, Wednesday, there's already a level of expectation.

The looks for this press run have been a mix of archival, fresh, and custom pieces. How do you make that choice? How important is it for you to create an archive for Mckenna?

According to recent reports, it kind of is a mix of what we’re able to source. Mckenna really wanted to pay homage to Joanna's character with that scene where she's like, "My stylist is always putting me in trees." She's like, "I wanna do a tree reference." And I'm like, "How in the world am I gonna find a fashion reference that's a tree that's not a costume?".

I love the challenge of sourcing the market, and so do the girls on my team. I think it was 2011 Phoebe Philo where Celine did some tree references in the collection. But just because we find it online doesn't mean that we can get it. So then it's reaching out to every vintage dealer, every rental house, asking, "Do you guys have anything like this?" And they might have it, but they're like, "It's already gone, someone has it." I ended up actually finding the Celine tree dress on the RealReal, and I bought it. I love RealReal.

Industry observers note that what is your approach to dressing different clients? For instance, you mentioned Sadie Sink earlier, can you walk me through how that process differs from Mckenna?

According to recent reports, it's very different between each girl. I let them set the pace. If they wanna be involved, great. If they just wanna show up to the fitting and not even know what's gonna be there, I try to accommodate whatever direction they wanna go. I have one client that literally last week has sent me over 200 references of dresses that she wants, and another girl that's like, “I really don't care. Whatever you tell me to wear, I'll wear it.”.

It has been revealed that every girl is different, and what makes my job so interesting is that it's not the same. Everyone has very different styles. I think the most important part of a job as a stylist is to keep their style true to them and not just force my style onto them. Mckenna's way more girly, Sadie is a little bit more casual, it’s just taking their style and elevating it a little bit.

Sources indicate that will you do any looks inspired by Mckenna’s character Maysilee? The looks have been mostly referential to things and people from past stories. Are there influences of Maysilee in the looks that fans haven't been able to pick up on because the film wasn’t out yet?

In a couple days, she’ll be in Miami for press, and she's wearing a very Maysilee inspired, purple Miu Miu dress that has a white collar. When she wears it, everyone's gonna be like, "Oh, that's Maysilee." She really wanted to have flowers and necklaces because Maysilee is really into jewelry, so it’s very light and flowery.

Can you break down the outfit for the Latest York City premiere?

We are doing the Mockingjay dress, the one with the wings, and that was another thing that I was very stumped on. I'm like, "What designer's gonna make these wings?" I had this woman in LA who does wings, she's done Halloween costumes and music videos.

Mckenna Grace in Pamella Roland.

According to recent reports, in the first fitting, I pulled this navy Pamella Roland gown. The fabric is really, really cool. It's like a shimmery kind of organza. I thought, "That's the right color,” but I wanted it to be strapless. I went back to Pamella Roland and they were like, "We can make it in strapless." Mckenna was very keen on having some sort of embellishment to replicate Katniss because she had screen printing on the gown and it kind of looks like wings in a way.

Industry observers note that pamella then drew all these CADs with diamond wings on it, and then we got the wings made. We did the final fitting and I almost started to cry. Her mom's taking videos and it's epic. It's so exciting because the fans were doing polls on what she's gonna wear to the premiere.

It's full circle, we started with the wedding dress, Mckenna did the fire gown, and then we ended with the Mockingjay dress.

What was the hardest look to pull together?

Mckenna Grace in custom Cong Tri.

I think design-wise, it was the fire gown.

Getting the fire printed on the fabric was really hard. I had a while back done a custom Cong Tri gown for Cami Mendes for the Masters of the Universe tour. It was like a gold beaded gown, and I remember I really liked the fabrics that they used for it.

Industry observers note that so when I was thinking of who could do this fire gown, I reached out to them first, and I'm like, "Can you guys do something that looks like a fire? Like, she's literally on fire." And they're like, "No. We don't think we can." And again, they were like, "Give us some time." They came back and noted, "We did all these testing on the fabric." I'm like, "Yeah, you did it. You did it.".

Recent findings suggest that what's really funny is we were at a fitting at Mckenna's house with the fire gown in a garment bag, and one of her friends stopped by. It was just a tip of the dress showing and her friend remarked, "Oh my God, you got a fire gown." Then I thought, "Okay, people are gonna get it.".

Sources indicate that hollow Knight: Silksong developer Team Cherry has announced it will host a 'Cherry Time Special Presentation' on 27th November, bringing more information to light about the game's first big DLC offering, Sea of Sorrows. We know that the free upgrade will be nautically-themed - hence the eponymous 'sea' - and will feature upcoming bosses, areas and so on, but other than that, information about what's coming is vague.

But it seems that's not all; as well as more information about the mysterious upgrade to the hit Metroidvania game, the studio has also declared "a bunch" of other "exciting announcements." Curious.

The Cherry Time Special Presentation will kick off at 7am PT / 10am ET / 3pm GMT / 4pm CEST. I'll embed the video below, so check back here at the time if you need a bookmark.

Recent findings suggest that recently, and more than a year after its initial release, physical versions of Hollow Knight: Silksong finally began arriving on players' doorsteps. Whilst these editions contained mostly expected information, there was an unforeseen mention of "free content packs" that would be arriving alongside the Sea of Sorrow DLC. Will we hear more about these as part of this latest showcase? We don't have too long to find out.

According to recent reports, it seems likely, though. "The world of Hollow Knight: Silksong will expand with free content packs," the booklet read in the physical editions. "Prepare for even more adventures filled with upcoming friends, new abilities, and new ferocious foes!" Team Cherry has repeatedly confirmed intends for post-launch Silksong support, but other than this upcoming DLC, we don't really know what that entails.

Additionally, Sea of Sorrow's original release window was a vague 2026 - will we see it shadowdrop as part of this stream? Stranger things have happened, especially in the world of Hollow Knight….

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 hasn't even been out for a week yet, and someone has already done the math on how many buildings in the whole of Leonida you can actually walk into. For those of you who are curious: it's 1,563 buildings.

That is frankly ridiculous. I don't think I've ever been inside 1,563 different buildings in my entire life, although I am a creature of habit, so that could explain things. The player who shared these stats, Aileos, does note that there are 5,588 buildings in total, so the enterable buildings only account for a fraction of that, just over 25%.

Recent findings suggest that there are some who will look at this with a glass-half-empty perspective, and I get it. This world is so cool, it's easy to want more of it, but as another player points out, "This would've sent us into psychosis a few years back". Sometimes it's better to focus on what we have rather than what we don't have. After all, how many buildings will you realistically enter in your GTA 6 playthrough? Probably not 1,563.

According to recent reports, we've spent the past week here in the PC Gamer Slack channel marvelling at just how many random encounters you can stumble across in GTA 6. Some of us have found sentient NPCs. One of us was actually recognised by a convenience store clerk who then asked to get robbed, and I think we've all seen videos of the furry rescue mission.

But just because this world already has loads of awesome activities, it doesn't mean we aren't hoping for more. A massive casino and go-kart track have been spotted by players, both of which have huge "Coming Soon" signs draped outside of them.

These buildings could be lying in wait for GTA 6 Online, or they could be added to singleplayer sometime in the future. Regardless, those are two more buildings that will potentially welcome players soon.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • “Cancer does change you,” Kate Middleton says, emotion clear in her voice.
  • According to Kensington Palace, which announced the film on Saturday, Heal is “a deeply personal new documentary from The Princess of Wales, exploring life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness.” It will air on the BBC in the UK on November 29, and in the US on NBCUniversal on November 30.
  • Heal follows Kate Middleton during her participation in one of the United Kingdom’s most demanding endurance events: The National Three Peaks Challenge, which she completed this summer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“Cancer does change you,” Kate Middleton says, emotion clear in her voice. “It changes your body, it changes you physically. But there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.” These words come not at as an Instagram post or at a public event. Instead, they're the voice-over in a previously unannounced documentary about the Princess of Wales and her life since she disclosed a diagnosis of cancer in 2024.

According to Kensington Palace, which announced the film on Saturday, Heal is “a deeply personal new documentary from The Princess of Wales, exploring life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness.” It will air on the BBC in the UK on November 29, and in the US on NBCUniversal on November 30.

Heal follows Kate Middleton during her participation in one of the United Kingdom’s most demanding endurance events: The National Three Peaks Challenge, which she completed this summer. In less than 24 hours, the princess climbed the three highest mountains in Scotland, England, and Wales: Ben Nevis (4,413 feet), Scafell Pike (3,209 feet), and Yr Wyddfa–Snowdon (3,559 feet). The undertaking wasn't just a personal effort, as it was also in support of the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, an organization that supports people living with cancer before, during, and after the disease.

The documentary will also support that organization, Kensington Palace notes, saying “All funds received through the documentary's distribution have been directed to The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity to help people living with and beyond cancer.” The Royal Marsden Hospital, at which Middleton received treatment, is also referenced in the film, as Middleton's brother, James, asks her “Isn’t it when you leave the Royal Marsden, you ring the bell?”.

But while many patients participate in the bell-ringing ritual at the conclusion of treatment, Middleton notes she missed out on that moment. “Yeah, but I didn’t ring the bell,” she replies. “So maybe this is your ringing of the bell,” James responded, suggesting her Three Peaks experience was that symbolic peal.

Industry observers note that while Prince William is no stranger to documentary work, nor are Prince Harry and wife Meghan Markle, this is Kate Middleton's first venture into the format. Perhaps to ease her into the project, Heal's Director of Photography is a face quite familiar to the Princess: Will Warr, the filmmaker behind her video announcement marking the end of her chemotherapy treatments.

“Through this documentary, The Princess hopes to help others navigate diagnosis, recovery and life beyond cancer and transform access to holistic cancer care which supports wellbeing, resilience and quality of life during and after diagnosis,” Kensington Palace says of Heal, a message underscored by Middleton's words in the trailer. “You know, healing is a journey. How to reconnect with the things you once knew and how to find a sense of hope and joy alongside uncertainty.”.

“It’s clear we're not meant to face life’s challenges alone,” the princess says as the trailer concludes. “Things can renew and grow. Often it is through pain that we realize that there is a greater beauty that lies beyond that.".

While there's no shortage of fans who are happy for the duo, there are a few disgruntled people who feel his win over Amber Glenn and others came because he lost his prosthetic during his final dance. It's a wild take that's making rounds, and I can't help but roll my eyes at it.

In a recent development, for those who didn't watch DWTS on Tuesday, November 24, on ABC or with a Disney+ subscription, Frech's mishap came during his freestyle dance, which began with him without his prosthetic on. Frech was supposed to slip it on during a quick change segment, and while it was on when he revealed his fresh look, it quickly fell to the floor. Frech continued to dance until pro dancer Alan Bersten could retrieve the leg, and after a brief pause, Frech reattached it and completed the routine.

Recent findings suggest that the moment received raucous applause from the in-house audience, and the judges awarded him perfect scores. Unfortunately, comments like the one below have since been floating around X, with some arguing Frech received sympathy votes and calling fans ableist for not penalizing him for the incident:.

Ezra wanted to be viewed the same as everyone else. Sorry but if that were the case, Amber would’ve won tonight. Ezra won cause his prosthetic fell off during his freestyle so people voted him out of sympathy & cause he was crying/bleeding after. That in itself is ableism.

I can't help but take a deep sigh when reading this take, and admittedly, I'm not the only one who has taken matter this person. With that noted, if there are more people out there who quietly believe or think that Ezra's disability is what pushed him across the finish line to be the latest person to win Dancing with the Stars, let me just point out a couple of details.

Recent findings suggest that to chalk Ezra Frech's win up to his final dance of the season discredits a run that was one of the best we've seen this entire season. He was never at the bottom of the leaderboard and was even at the top for a few weeks. Frech never had an off week, not once, which is the type of resilience we expect from Olympic athletes.

Industry observers note that now, looking at the numbers, you'll see Amber Glenn did just as well, and even beat out Ezra for more than a few weeks. As we learned this season, however, DWTS is just as much a popularity contest as it is a dance competition. If Amber should win on scores alone, Jenna Dewan shouldn't have left, and Harry Shum Jr. would've been holding that Mirrorball trophy.

In a recent development, if Ezra Frech gained additional votes in Dancing with the Stars' finale after his freestyle performance, it wasn't out of sympathy. That would imply the dance fell to disaster after he lost his prosthetic, and that simply wasn't the case. Frech not only finished the dance, he completed the routine hardly missing a beat.

If the fans feel Frech's win wasn't justified, then maybe it is time to push for Sharna Burgess' campaign to limit fans to only ten votes. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • As World of Warcraft: Forever players dived into the game, they swiftly discovered a specific weapon enchant that took area of effect spells to a whole other level.
  • The enchantment in question was Revelation - a fresh addition to the game included as part of the new trade good reputations.
  • So for example, let's say you're a druid casting the Hurricane spell.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As World of Warcraft: Forever players dived into the game, they swiftly discovered a specific weapon enchant that took area of effect spells to a whole other level. Sadly, with a sudden hotfix last night, this particular use case for the enchant has been removed.

The enchantment in question was Revelation - a fresh addition to the game included as part of the new trade good reputations. What it does is simple: when you fail to deal a critical strike with a spell, the next spell hit is guaranteed to do so. What made this particularly powerful is that the buff also worked with continuous area of effect spells, meaning an early instance of the spell not crit-ing would result in the remaining damage hits all dealing critical damage.

So for example, let's say you're a druid casting the Hurricane spell. This is a channel spell with a total of 10 seconds of cast time. Every second, it deals damage. If the first instance of damage at the one second mark doesn't crit, the remaining nine instances of damage would all crit. This resulted in absurd amounts of damage, and made players of druids, warlocks, and mages very happy.

While strong enchantments are often pricey, this was notably cheap, due to the low-cost of resources used to create it and the low requirements to learn it. As such, people were spending a handful of gold for an early game enchantment that was being actively used all the way into the end game.

Industry observers note that it was admittedly a tad too strong, and the effect triggered on AOE spells was almost certainly an unintended effect of the enchantment. Last night, the fun came to an end. Now, the effect is used up as intended in long-casted spells. So going back to the example given, if the first instance of damage on Hurricane doesn't crit, then the second one still will. However, this will use up the effect, and the third instance of damage will revert to regular ol' damage numbers. It also seems as though it Revelation can't trigger more than once during a single channeled spell.

In a recent development, this is the latest in a string of ongoing quickfire bug fixes and game adjustments being made to World of Warcraft: Forever. The devs have been continuously updating the game in an attempt to curb certain gold farms, following the discovery of a particularly lucrative Blackmaw Hold gold exploit. The dev team has expressed some interesting ideas for the game longterm, including a desire to kill best-in-slot gear.

According to recent reports, “Oh, it feels good [to hear about the support]. I haven’t seen much. I have seen some, like, ‘Where is Cameron? We want to see more of Cameron,'” Williams, 40, exclusively told Us about the public outcry over her character appearing in fewer scenes. “As an artist, you are being really sensitive about your stuff so to see it be loved and appreciated [is meaningful].”.

Williams reflected on how she has found herself connecting with Cameron.

Sources indicate that “We work really hard as artists — and for me in particular — this isn’t the easiest job for me. Being away from home, there’s so much that I can relate to with Cameron, and I understand her on so many levels,” she explained. “Being a foreigner, being an outsider and being the only Black cast member. These are real life things that I actually can genuinely say that I embody. I understand it’s my reality as much as it is hers.”.

According to recent reports, based on Jilly Cooper‘s novel of the same name, Rivals follows a feud between two men fighting for control of a television station in 1980s Britain. Cameron, who was introduced in season 1, rapidly gets involved through her past affair with Tony (David Tennant), her eventual romance with Rupert (Alex Hassell) and her professional drive, which initially put her at odds with Declan (Aidan Turner).

Cameron was front and center when the series originally premiered in 2025. By the time season 2 returned earlier this year, eagle-eyed audience members noticed that having such a large ensemble cast led to Cameron being featured — to their frustration.

“It’s just really nice to see the love and to feel it. Thank you for sharing that with me,” Williams added. “That’s just for Disney and Hulu and everybody to hear. I don’t know how that’ll go possibly in season 3, I think Cameron speaks not just for Black women though but for all women. There’s so many women who are so inspired by her.”.

Recent findings suggest that as a result, Williams is hoping Cameron’s story will keep getting explored, adding, “It’s kind of interesting and cool to see how she’s affecting so many different women. She transcends not just color but age too. There’s teenagers who come up to me and they talk about how empowering and how inspiring she is for them. That feels pretty damn good because as an artist, you want to pick roles that matter, that means something, and that move people where people can see themselves.”.

Sources indicate that there's been a massive gap between newly introduced entries in The Witcher series, and for The Witcher 4, developer CD Projekt Red aims to make it the GTA 6 of the series, with a noticeable leap in quality. In its Q3 earnings call, the studio claims it has been inspired by the technological and gameplay advancements Rockstar Games has made with GTA 6--especially when compared to 2013's GTA 5--and hopes players will feel the same way when they jump into The Witcher 4. "First of all, obviously this is a call about us, not about Rockstar," CDPR joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski (via Eurogamer). "But I do understand the connection here. Having said that, I'm not going to make a deep-dive and a full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6. But of course we did look at the game; we did see the differences. We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4--I think so, yes. It's been 11 years; we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4c1rokekgnY When The Witcher 3: The Wild Hunt was first released in 2015, it was hailed for raising the bar for open-world adventure games. Its side-quests were singled out for being narratively dense, full of micro-consequences, and on par with the main campaign missions. In the years since, numerous open-world games have used The Witcher 3 as a blueprint, with notable examples being the Assassin's Creed trilogy of Origins, Odyssey, and Valhalla alongside Sony's Horizon Zero Dawn and Ghost of Tsushima. Eleven years later, that bar has been raised again with GTA 6, which offers emergent, player-driven open-world chaos through multiple systems. The world of The Witcher is naturally very different from the consumerism-focused setting of GTA 6, but if The Witcher 4 builds on its predecessor's strengths and adds more nuance to those gameplay mechanics, we could be in for something special. CDPR also said it's trying to make The Witcher 4 more appealing to mainstream audiences, but it hasn't detailed exactly how it aims to do that. "Our games are different, and they require a certain different approach--we just do things differently than they do. But in terms of the ultimate effect, in terms of breaking out to the mass market awareness: This is for sure something we consider pivotal to whatever we're going to do with our marketing campaigns in the future," Nowakowski said. Presently, over 500 people are working on The Witcher 4, and CDPR has signed a marketing agreement with PlayStation for the game ahead of its targeted 2028 release. The studio is also chipping away at Cyberpunk 2, but after the launch of GTA 6, the game's creative director joked about canceling it, saying Rockstar's game set a high standard for open-world games.

#108774. Why did Rockstar Games make empathy a key mechanic in GTA 6? "Because it's fun" indicates head of development Rob Nelson

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1508 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

Why did Rockstar Games make empathy a key mechanic in GTA 6? "Because it's fun" indicates head of development Rob Nelson

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1508 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There's been plenty of chatter about Grand Theft Auto 6's 'honour system', so to speak, implemented here via what the game calls your Criminal Profile.
  • Our own Dom just wrote that they prefer to turn its notifications off, for instance, in favour of fully soaking into the immersion.
  • Recent findings suggest that some of that is genuinely interesting - I'm dubious as to whether that's really what this system is doing, for a start.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's been plenty of chatter about Grand Theft Auto 6's 'honour system', so to speak, implemented here via what the game calls your Criminal Profile.

Our own Dom just wrote that they prefer to turn its notifications off, for instance, in favour of fully soaking into the immersion. Personally I quite like the pop-ups - I find the act of figuring out systems and how they're manipulated almost as fun as the games they're a part of. And pop-ups or no, the fact that GTA 6 can arguably be portrayed as 'rewarding' empathy and 'discouraging' the series' famous rampages of mass violence has sparked a fair bit of debate.

Recent findings suggest that some of that is genuinely interesting - I'm dubious as to whether that's really what this system is doing, for a start. Is it incentivising and disincentivising certain in-game behaviour, or just putting a label on it? And then, actually: does the act of labelling "psycho" behaviour alone actually become a disincentivising factor in itself?

Industry observers note that either way, until now Rockstar hasn't stated a great deal about why, exactly, this system - seen by some as one that builds empathy into GTA's chaotic world - was implemented in the first place. But during an interview I had with Rob Nelson, Rockstar Games' head of development, just before GTA 6's launch earlier this month, a little more on that came to light.

Recent findings suggest that A little context is necessary here: Nelson's response was actually following a question I had about the overall approach to design that Rockstar took, and how its wider themes and intentions came about. As a part of that, he turned to this system - and how, in a way, it exists here because of the work the studio simply didn't want to leave behind after Red Dead Redemption 2.

Nelson explained that this all began when the team was in the early phase of exploring what type of game GTA 6 would be, in 2015 and 2016, while much of the studio was still working full-tilt on RDR2 - a game which itself didn't release until late 2018. The team was looking to "build up the sophistication of the NPC population, and also allow for more player choice than we had [before], and more options in terms of the way you interact with the world beyond just violence," Nelson told me.

Recent findings suggest that the idea would be that "it's still a world of violence - but you could threaten somebody by aiming a gun at them and just robbing them, and they have a chance to comply. So you don't have to beat them to death to get their money." Ideas that were "simple things" in principle, he noted, "but they create a lot more work in terms of development of the sophistication of the systems.".

Then, as systems were gradually implemented, it became a question of "trying to marry up what you're doing in the open world with who we're saying you are in the narrative - more than we had, I would say, previously, in Red Dead 2." It's here where the system now referred to as the Criminal Profile started to form.

The thinking turned to "the nature of 'honour', which wasn't always a part of it" with Red Dead Redemption 2, Nelson continued, "but became part of it as we were working on this story and finding that the 'redemption arc' didn't feel so good when it was foisted upon you - and feelings that we had playing Red Dead sort of early on." (Those feelings, primarily, were around getting you to invest in a gang led by Dutch Van der Linde, who was fundamentally unlikable from the off - or plain "crazy", as Nelson put it. The implementation of more player choices and agency was part of Rockstar's way to build investment in Arthur, even as he followed Dutch.).

That meant moving the choices away from key story moments, where many games tend to put them. Instead, Rockstar built a system that ran alongside the story via smaller, moment-to-moment choices you might make. "We tried to take all of those off the main flow and make them optional. So again, they're a choice.".

According to recent reports, "Usually they involve some form of slight sacrifice or more effort on the part of the player," he added. The hope, then, was that you as a player would both "feel something", and ultimately also feel "you got the outcome that you deserved.".

That was the initial thinking behind this kind of system as a whole. Coming to GTA 6, it then combined with a wider desire to "evolve" Grand Theft Auto as both the team's storytelling and the available technology matured. "You're thinking about story and character set, but we're also thinking about what we want to do with GTA as a series, and how you want to evolve it," Nelson remarked.

"I think as the resolution goes up, it sort of asks different upcoming questions," he continued. "As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up, and obviously the sophistication of the mechanics. So it just naturally flowed that we give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun', because it's fun.".

According to recent reports, "It's fun for some people like myself to just sort of role-play in the world, and be in the world, and restraint becomes something you hadn't thought about," he continued. That tied back into the more sophisticated NPCs and reactions the team were making.

In a recent development, "If you think about the NPCs, even back to [GTA] 5, you would draw a weapon - first of all, they didn't react if you drew an invisible shotgun out of nowhere, or a rocket launcher," he remarked. "They don't react unless you aim it, and then they flee in terror, and you're just sort of this demigod stomping through the world, you know? And that's fun, but for how long?

"The team then started thinking of ways to build a bit more sustained enjoyment from it. "What if you can't do that?" Nelson continued. What if, instead of whipping an RPG out of nowhere, "you have to call your car. You have to pop a car trunk and get it, and now I'm walking, and now people are noticing, but they're sort of sidling away, and it's more believable. And then they're still fleeing in terror, but then there's people who also have guns, and they're shooting at you, or you try to hold somebody up and they pull a gun, or they grab it, and then you have to deal with them.

Industry observers note that "And then, he continued, "you choose. You're trying to jack somebody off a motorcycle, and they pull a gun on you, and you have to blow their head off and it's like, 'You shouldn't have made me do that!' And so then it has more meaning, and it's more funny in a way when it's a little bit more pointed. And you can still go on those rampages and basically smash your Criminal Profile until it breaks and then you enter this irredeemable state, which basically says 'I reject your criminal profile system! I don't want it.'".

Industry observers note that that Irredeemable profile level, for what it's worth, was another element born of Red Dead Redemption 2. "We had that with Red Dead, where people would sort of have low honour, and then 'greet' their way back up to high honour. And so this was an attempt of sorts of [making something] for people that just want to go crazy and almost opt out of the system. They can opt out of it - and you can also turn off the notifications in the system.".

It has been revealed that it's notable, in fact, just how interlinked the thinking was with GTA 6 and Red Dead Redemption 2. As Nelson put it at one point: "There was maybe more emotional resonance in the story of RDR2 than we had had, certainly in a GTA before. So we liked that idea." What Rockstar did with GTA 6 was then in a way a natural next step. "We didn't necessarily come to GTA 6 going: 'We must have emotional resonance,' but all of those things combine. It's more that those systems and that element of player choice and agency, and the way that affected the narrative, was a hard thing to ignore and walk away from.".

We'll have much more like this from our interview with Nelson very soon, so do look out for that on Eurogamer over the coming days. In the meantime, we've a handy guide explaining exactly how GTA 6's Criminal Profile system works and how to change, raise, or lower that profile if you're in need of a deep dive into how it all really works.

Not every Black Friday or Cyber Monday deal is as sweet as it seems. With electronics and tech in particular, you could be buying last year's model that has actually been on sale since the summer—and was maybe a better price a few months ago. Here’s how to avoid impulse buying a misleading Black Friday “deal” and make sure you’re getting the best bang for your buck.

Recent findings suggest that when you see products like food, clothes, or home goods with a massive "Black Friday" or "Cyber Monday" tag slapped on them, it's probably safe to take advantage of that deal. Chances are it's the same exact product you'd find on other days of the year. The same can’t be mentioned for a TV, laptop, and other tech deals, where the product itself is constantly being upgraded.

Because tech is always evolving, and retailers want to move inventory before fresh models come out, electronics are especially susceptible to a practice known as "price anchoring." That's when retailers mark up prices in the weeks leading up to Black Friday, before "slashing" those prices back down, giving the appearance of a deal that isn't really a deal at all. Still, when you see that marked-up number, aka the "price anchor," you might get tricked into thinking you're saving money when you're not. There's also the false sense of urgency that gets created. It's second nature to assume that anything labeled "deal" won’t last long—even when this so-called deal price has actually been going on since the summer.

According to recent reports, price anchoring isn't even unique to Black Friday. The nonprofit Consumers’ Checkbook tracked prices at 25 major retailers over 33 weeks in 2022 and found that more than half the items tracked were offered at false discounts every week or almost every week. Less common, but also worth noting, is a known practice of "derivative" or retailer-exclusive models produced specifically for the holiday shopping season. These versions often feature cheaper components, fewer features, or lower specifications than their regular counterparts. A 55-inch TV from a reputable brand might look identical to the year-round model, but it could have a lower refresh rate, inferior panel technology, or fewer HDMI ports.

In the same vein, that "amazing deal" on a laptop might come with last year's processor, or a smartphone that's about to be replaced. The problem isn't that the tech is an older model, but again, it's that it probably has been at this low a price, or lower, since the summer. Alternatively, some deeply discounted electronics are refurbished units or open-box returns that have been repackaged. Again, while this isn't necessarily a bad thing, impulse buyers may not fully realize what they're buying.

Sources indicate that the key phrasing here is impulse buying. Events like Black Friday are psychologically engineered to trigger impulse purchases. Limited-time offers, countdown clocks, and "while supplies last" warnings create artificial urgency. When you're caught up in the moment, it's easy to convince yourself you need a latest tablet, smartwatch, or gaming console, even if you hadn't considered buying one before.

To avoid a low-key scam, do your research. The easiest way to tell that you’re getting the correct product is by checking the model or serial number. And with online shopping, finding and double-checking those numbers is quick and easy. In addition, don't just compare prices—compare specs. Look at processor speeds, RAM, storage capacity, screen resolution, refresh rates, and connectivity options. A $300 laptop isn't a deal if a slightly more expensive model offers significantly better performance that will last longer.

It has been revealed that if you do see a deal that catches your eye, it could pay to wait. Cyber Monday, post-Christmas sales, and even January clearances often feature electronics deals that rival or beat Black Friday prices, all without the famous chaos and pressure. Then again, you risk more “out-of-stock” results if you wait, so the risk is up to you, depending on the popularity of the item you’re eyeing (and how badly you want it).

The bottom line: Don’t fall victim to a falsely advertised lower-quality product, and do a little research to find actually good deals ahead of time.

The Dancing With the Stars season 35 cast left it all on the ballroom floor one last time — including runners-up Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov.

“It really was, like, a very triumphant feeling for me,” Glenn, 27, told Extra after the finale on Tuesday, November 24, reflecting on coming in second place to Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach. “I couldn’t ask for a better result.”.

Glenn and Pashkov, 40, performed a judges’ choice dance, an instant dance and the fan-favorite freestyle, earning perfect 30s from judges Carrie Ann Inaba, Bruno Tonioli and Derek Hough for all three performances. At the end of the night, the pair were tied on the leaderboard with Frech, 21, and Karagach, 33, as well as fellow finalists Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas.

Though she didn’t take home the mirrorball trophy herself, Glenn was proud that the victory stayed in the family for Pashkov and Karagach.

It has been revealed that “From day one, we all met up, had a little dinner over at their house and we stated, ‘We wanna go 1-2,'” she said. “And we didn’t specify, like, whatever happens, happens, but the fact that we came in here and we both got those perfect scores. We both did everything we could and it was truly in the hands of the people at home. I’m really proud of what we did and I’m really, really happy that Team USA took it home.”.

In a separate interview with Variety, Glenn opened up about the biggest lessons she’s learned from her DWTS experience.

In a recent development, “Being able to work so closely with someone else, being able to trust. We have tour, I’m excited to keep dancing and keep learning. This is a part of my life and really a highlight of my life,” she gushed.

While the intense — and at times, scandalous — season has come to a close, several of the celebrity contestants have spoken about maintaining their close bonds outside of the show.

According to recent reports, “I’ll miss getting to see everyone at the rehearsal studio. I’ll miss getting lunch with Dani after practice,” Frech told Cosmopolitan in an interview published on Monday, November 23. “I’ll miss getting the opportunity to commit myself to something like this so entirely. And I’m gonna miss the show days.”.

Sources indicate that he continued, “You become so close to everybody, and you spend so much time around these people, and then all of a sudden, it’s going to end. But the good thing is that these people are still going to be in my life. I’m still going to hang out with Dani, and I’m still going to see Connor [Wood] whenever I can, and we’ll get lunch with Guillermo [Rodriguez]. These are people I’ll be with forever.”.

Wood, for his part, reflected in the same interview about how the reality TV competition experience has felt “like a study abroad trip.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that PC modders are racing to get GTA 6 playable on PC after the leak of the game's complete Xbox build, but so far it doesn't look too promising. GTA 6 publisher Take-Two Interactive and developer Rockstar Games haven't been sitting idle either, as one of the leads behind the Project Leonida Discord group claimed in now-deleted social media posts that they were stepping away from the mammoth task of getting GTA 6 to run on PC. Project Leonida has also been taken down, but it's not the only group trying to get GTA 6 running outside of PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ble-JJxBBGA None of these groups have succeeded yet, and as Twitter user Chasm detailed online, maybe relying heavily on AI tools isn't the way to go. Dev streams have been full of users leveraging generative AI tools to do something, with several prompts being absolute gems of wishful thinking. Here's a snippet of what people have been throwing at Google's Antigravity, while butchering the English language: Continue working and do apply ever part of the code make no mistakes You need todo one thing at a time not a little bit of everything we need all the game start like the rockstar launch so on that stuff, not in game stuff yet work faster there has to be a faster way to iterate than this Even with an army of enthusiasts throwing prompts and cash at generative AI, a copied version of GTA 6 still seems far out of reach. Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick commented in March that the idea of using AI and simply pushing a button to make a hit game was "laughable," and he referenced the music industry, which is grappling with a flood of AI slop to top streaming platforms. "Right now [in music] there are programs that allow you to put out a prompt and get a professionally recorded song spit back out at you. It sounds like a song, but I defy you to listen to it more than once. It's great to send as a greeting card to your partner on their birthday, but that's about it," Zelnick said. Whatever progress is made in the GTA 6 PC port scene, don't expect it to last long before Take-Two's lawyers pounce. The publisher hasn't shied away from protecting its IP in the past, and takedown notices for any future GTA 6-related projects seem likely. Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto 6Â contains a surprising but cool cameo hidden near the very end of the game’s main story. So when I got a chance to chat with Rockstar’s head of production, Rob Nelson, about GTA 6 ahead of the game’s launch, I had to ask about this moment, how it came about, and what it means for the character.

In a recent development, but uh… major spoilers. Seriously, if you’re a significant GTA nerd and love to be surprised, turn around right now and stop reading. You’ll thank me later when you reach this point and get to experience it unspoiled. For those who don’t care or who can’t resist the siren’s call of secrets being revealed, keep scrolling past the warning. Just don’t yell at me later!

As you approach the final missions in the game, Jason and Lucia start working with Giorgio, a very rich shipping magnate who works with Eastern European criminals to smuggle drugs across the ocean on his substantial ships. And things aren’t going well, forcing Giorgio to work with Jason, Lucia, and others on a big, ambitious proposal to steal back all the cocaine confiscated by the Coast Guard as part of a large heist. But before they can pull off the heist, a higher-up from the big Balkan cartel Giorgio has been working with arrives to kill him for screwing up, but gives him one more chance to get back the coke. That badass hitman? Niko Bellic, the playable protagonist of 2008’s Grand Theft Auto IV.

Here’s the scene from GTA 6 in which he appears:.

I asked Nelson if they’d planned to include Niko from the start, and he tells me that they hadn’t. Instead, he told me that the cameo came about “very organically.”.

“[Early in development], we had Giorgio and we had him working with a sort of Balkan cartel,” explained Nelson. The GTA 6 boss further explained that this whole storyline was based on research they’d done about actual Italian shipping companies that allegedly smuggled drugs for various gangs in South America. Apparently, a boat run by such a company was carrying 20 tons of coke when it was raided by U.S. officials. That number should sound familiar to anyone who has played the later missions of GTA 6, as that’s the amount of coke seized by the Coast Guard in the game.Â.

“Giorgio is not really a criminal. He’s a sort of wealthy shipping magnate who’s in league with these criminals,” said Nelson.

“But it was sort of that same [real-world] idea. And then we needed someone from the Balkan cartel to show up. It just grew very organically, and it’s like, well, who would he be working with from the Balkan end of the organization? When Giorgio fucks up, who’s going to come down to deal with him? And I got an idea.”.

It has been revealed that nelson states Niko’s story was sort of “left open” after the events of GTA IV.Â “He’s still kicking around. He’s still in play,” he told Kotaku. Nelson also confirmed original voice actor Michael Holick returned for the role. When I asked if it was nice to have him back and work with him again, Nelson responded with a smile: “Very much, yeah.”Â.

Sources indicate that I asked Nelson if this cameo confirms anything about which ending is canon in GTA IV, and Nelson wouldn’t say one way or the other and pointed out that nothing Niko states or does in either cutscene indicates a specific canon ending for that game. He did confirm that Niko will be going back to Liberty City after all this and that it’s been his home since GTA IV.Â.

There’s one more great detail included in this cameo moment. After the cutscene ends, players hear the mission-complete jingle from GTA IV play instead of one of GTA 6‘s various mission-complete jingles. According to Nelson, that was a “late addition.”.

“For a long time it was like a normal [GTA 6] stinger, and we played it and…” Nelson made an meh face. “I got on with Yvonne and stated, ‘Can we put the [mimics the GTA IV mission complete jingle] in there?'” And they did, which was a wonderful touch to an already amazing moment.Â.

Recent findings suggest that when we talked about Niko Bellic in GTA 6, Nelson did admit that he hoped “it stays secret for a bit.” Sadly, a lot of people rushed through GTA 6 and posted videos of Niko last week, less than three days after the game’s launch. Welp.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Atari Homebrew Awards, an annual celebration of latest games developed for old systems by the people who love them both, has been cancelled after eight years of operation—and yes, it's because of AI.

It has been revealed that "As you may know, the landscape of retro game development changed dramatically this year with the massively increased capabilities of LLMs. More and more games have incorporated AI elements into their development chain and now have the capability to create full games without writing a single line of code," Atari Homebrew Awards host James, aka ZeroPage Homebrew, wrote on the Atari Age forums.

"Keeping up with the large number of AI-assisted game development had become increasingly difficult as this year wore on, with some developers even releasing multiple games a week with the aid of AI. This flood of new AI games forced me to re-evaluate the way games were qualified and judged for the upcoming AHAs.

Recent findings suggest that "The Atari Homebrew Awards were now challenged to make sure the work of human developers were still honoured amongst the fresh fully computer-coded games. I was not at all interested in giving awards to the output of large language models, only to humans who coded their own games, but I swiftly discovered that this was going to be more difficult than I thought.".

James stated he discovered last week that "a large majority" of developers were using AI in some capacity to make their games, from testing to wholesale game creation, "without one typed line of code." That left two options: Disallow any and all AI usage in the Atari Homebrew Awards competition, which James said would disqualify a large number of "extremely talented coders" who used AI in some very minor way, or let it slide and choose some sort of arbitrary dividing line between what is and isn't allowed—or just let it go entirely and allow everything, including fully vibe-coded games.

James remarked he wasn't interested in that, which meant he needed to settle on how much AI usage would be allowable—and also how to determine if AI was used at all, since some developers are better at disclosure than others. That, naturally, led to the worry that developers could be subject to "false positives and possible witch hunts," something that's already a problem in mainstream game development.

This is an extremely upsetting conclusion for this event because honouring all the hard work the community put into these games is always a highlight of my year.

Ultimately, James decided there was no practical way forward, although he did leave open the possibility of a return someday. "This is an extremely upsetting conclusion for this event because honouring all the hard work the community put into these games is always a highlight of my year," he wrote. "I know many others feel the same way and I hope to be able to continue this tradition in the coming years as things settle into a upcoming normal.".

Keep up to date with the most vital stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

As we noted in July, debates over "acceptable" levels of AI use are cropping up all over the open source development scene: Some are drawing hard lines against it for principled and/or practical reasons, yet its popularity is growing explosively because, frankly, you don't need to know what you're doing in order to do it—as long as you're not too concerned with doing it well.

The Atari Homebrew Awards isn't the first such event to fall victim to the AI flood. Earlier in November, the Australian STEM Videogame Challenge, a "free national videogame development competition for students," announced that the 2026 event will be its last because "the rapid and complex rise of generative AI in game development [made] it harder to judge what students made themselves," and thus undercut the whole purpose of the program: Encouraging kids to learn how to code.

It has been revealed that I've been looking forward to seeing Sir Patrick Stewart return as Professor Charles Xavier in Avengers: Doomsday, especially knowing he'll be sharing the screen with Sir Ian McKellen again. The two actors have been part of the X-Men franchise for more than 25 years, and I can't imagine the flick without them. Although after Stewart's death in October, his final appearance will carry considerably more emotional weight than anyone originally anticipated. Now Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige and directors Joe and Anthony Russo are opening up about Stewart's last day on set for the upcoming Marvel movie, and I'm already getting emotional.

Industry observers note that speaking with Entertainment Weekly, Feige recalled a moment when the legendary actor addressed the crew after completing his work. Nobody knew for certain what it would mean at the time, but looking back, it sounds like Stewart knew he was saying goodbye. Marvel's head honcho revealed:.

Industry observers note that well, that got me. Stewart died at 86 on Oct. 29, making Doomsday his final on-screen performance. Knowing he apparently recognized the significance of that moment makes the story particularly heartbreaking.

In a recent development, I've always admired Stewart's ability to bring such extraordinary warmth and humanity to Charles Xavier. Even when the X-Men movies weren't particularly great, his presence could make a scene work. Sources indicate that the director also revealed that Stewart was dealing with significant health challenges while filming. According to Russo, the actor's determination to deliver the performance was evident to everyone around him. And it wasn't easy watching someone they admired push himself so hard. He continued:.

Recent findings suggest that it was clear that he was struggling with his health, and he worked so hard to deliver a performance and a presence — for us as directors, for his other actors, for the crew. You could see it wasn’t just the effort of a regular actor showing up and delivering that kind of presence and performance and experience for others, collaboration. It was someone who was really being challenged in a very deep way on a health level, showing up and doing that. For him to have muscled through and delivered the performance that he did in that movie, and the experience that he delivered for all of us as collaborators, it made it intensely emotional.

According to recent reports, I have a feeling that sentiment will carry over to audiences when the film finally arrives. Stewart first portrayed Xavier in the 2000s X-Men, eventually becoming one of the franchise's most recognizable faces. He returned for several sequels, delivered a particularly devastating performance in 2017's Logan, and later surprised MCU fans with an appearance in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness.

Sources indicate that now, more than a quarter-century after his first appearance, he'll be returning alongside McKellen's Magneto. Joe Russo revealed that the longtime friends share an emotional scene about forgiveness, which could be especially difficult to watch under the circumstances.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Another detail from the interview makes this farewell even sadder. Stewart was reportedly offered a role in Avengers: Secret Wars as well, but chose to appear only in Doomsday. Feige also confirmed that Marvel is working on a tribute to the actor for the upcoming release.

I can't help thinking about how many people grew up with Stewart's Professor X, myself included. His portrayal helped define what latest superhero movies could accomplish emotionally long before cinematic universes became the norm.

Knowing his final day involved such a heartfelt farewell to the people around him makes me appreciate his commitment even more. Whatever happens to Charles Xavier in Doomsday, I'm grateful Stewart got one last opportunity to play him.

Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters December 18 as part of the 2026 movie release schedule. I'll be bringing tissues.

And hark, just in the nick of time, PlayStation Plus' monthly games for December have been revealed, with some skating, spooking, and dragon baubles.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You can cancel your Prime subscription via web browser by first logging into your Amazon account. Amazon has a Cancel Your Prime Membership button on its support page to launch the process, or you can follow the steps detailed on Amazon's page:.

Head to Amazon.com in your web browser.

Hover over the Accounts & Lists menu on the top-right of the window, then select the Prime Membership option.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

Note that Amazon requires a bunch of clicks to finalize your cancellation, giving you lots of “opportunities” to change your mind.

Open the Amazon Shopping app on your mobile device.

Click the three horizontal lines on the bottom right.

Under Shop by Category, select Prime.

On the top bar, slide all the way to the end and select Help.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

According to recent reports, as mentioned, closing your account will immediately end your access. Amazon also offers you the option to pause your benefits and billing temporarily instead of canceling them completely. Either way, your Amazon account is still active—you simply won’t have Prime benefits.

Sources indicate that finally, if you have other subscriptions connected to your Prime account, those will end when your billing is up. And if you signed up for Prime through the Android mobile shopping app or the Prime Video Android app, you’ll have to go through Google Subscription to manage your membership.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Recent findings suggest that nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, Nov. 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Sources indicate that yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.
